feedback_interpretation: Recent m81 outcomes weakened smooth loading interpolation: 7d402b3fad455f06fe68 completed at 9.74 mL, whereas ce11189a0e59d1798306, eb6c235e6ed90084bfc9 and 390d6dfe33afc329fb17 were near 16.7–17.4 mL at nearby recorded conditions. I therefore sample connected strong-solvent and intermediate m81 points rather than applying a broad correction. m115 showed a lower-loading pure-EA completion of 8.65 mL, a midpoint value of 13.26 mL and an upper-loading value of 12.26 mL, reinforcing loading-specific nonlinearity but making further m115 labels less informative than remaining gaps. m33 confirmed loading-dependent completion at 10/1, while m166 retained a positive weak-solvent loading contrast. The predicted m145 onset maximum and m187 onset decline were not supported, so this batch reduces further sampling of those shapes. The measured m156 completion growth and m155 nonmonotonicity remain useful, so I test their missing intermediate regions. The large m212 loading contrast is now treated as scaffold-specific and receives stronger-solvent controls.
batch_rationale: The first 20 selections form connected local experiments: m81, m33, m166, m156, m155, m91, m212 and m92 each add matched solvent or loading information that can distinguish smooth response from endpoint-specific or nonlinear behavior. m203 and m142 extend unresolved boundary responses. The final seven selections repair broad, high-width model regions in nitro, ketone, ester, alcohol and heteroatom-rich scaffolds where prior measured labels showed large scale errors or sharp weak-solvent transitions. This combines local curvature repair with structural exploration while retaining diversity in molecular interactions, loading amount and solvent protocol. The labels should improve generalization by teaching conditional relationships rather than only correcting isolated predictions.
